info.title: DeepX API
info.description:
DeepX Public API V1.

## Changelog

**v1.0.0 (2026-03-24)**

- Initial release

## General API Information

- **Time Format**: All timestamps are in milliseconds (ms) by default.
- **Data Order**: Data is returned in chronological order, unless noted otherwise. Here is how the `startTime` and `endTime` parameters work:
  * Without `startTime` or `endTime`, returns the most recent items up to the `limit`.
  * With `startTime`, returns oldest items from `startTime` up to the `limit`.
  * With `endTime`, returns most recent items up to `endTime` and the `limit`.
  * With both, behaves like `startTime` but does not exceed `endTime`.
- **Pagination**: Historical data is paginated using `cursor` and `limit`. All paginated responses include `nextCursor` and `hasNext` metadata:
  * `nextCursor`: The ID of the oldest record in the current page. Pass this as `cursor` in the next request to fetch the next (older) page. `null` when there are no more records.
  * `hasNext`: `true` if more records are available beyond the current page. Stop paginating when `hasNext` is `false` (equivalent to the returned array length being `< limit`).
  * When combining with `startTime`/`endTime`, all three filters apply together:
    - With `cursor` and `endTime`, returns items after `cursor` and before `endTime` up to the `limit`.
    - With `cursor` and `startTime`, returns items after `cursor` and after `startTime` up to the `limit`.
    - With `cursor`, `startTime`, and `endTime`, returns items after `cursor` and between `startTime` and `endTime` up to the `limit`.
  * When `cursor` points to a record earlier than `startTime`, all candidate records fall before the time window. The response returns an empty `items` array with `nextCursor: null` and `hasNext: false`.

get.description: Retrieves a unified portfolio summary for a subaccount, including net account value, deposit/borrow totals, collateral, and risk metrics.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: The subaccount address.

schema.description: An Ethereum-compatible address in 0x-prefixed hex format (20 bytes).

A unified portfolio summary for a subaccount. Includes net account value, total deposit/borrow values, initial and maintenance collateral, margin requirements, the Unified Maintenance Margin Ratio (uniMMR), and the Unified Initial Margin Ratio (uniIMR).

subaccount.description: The subaccount address this portfolio summary belongs to.

equity.description: Net account value in USD. Calculated as total deposits minus total borrows minus accrued borrow interest, plus unrealized PnL across all open positions and unsettled funding payments.

totalDepositsUsd.description: Total USD value of all assets deposited in the subaccount.

totalBorrowsUsd.description: Total USD value of all borrowed assets.

totalCollateral.description: Total Collateral Value (maintenance-level). Equals the sum of all Maintenance Asset Values (MAV) plus unrealized PnL and unsettled funding payments.

initCollateral.description: Total Initial Collateral Value. Equals the aggregate Initial Asset Value (IAV) of all deposited assets. Used to determine how much collateral is available for opening new positions or borrowing.

maintMarginReq.description: Maintenance Margin Requirement (MMReq). The minimum collateral the account must maintain across all open positions to avoid liquidation.

initMarginReq.description: Initial Margin Requirement (IMReq). The total initial-level, risk-weighted value of all liabilities — borrowed assets, open positions, and open orders. Used as the gating threshold for opening new positions.

availableMargin.description: Available margin for new positions and borrowing. Calculated as `max(initCollateral - initMarginReq, 0)`. Divide by a market's Initial Margin Ratio (IMR) to estimate the maximum openable notional value.

uniMMR.description: Unified Maintenance Margin Ratio. Calculated as `totalCollateral / maintMarginReq`. When this falls below `1`, the account is subject to liquidation.

uniIMR.description: Unified Initial Margin Ratio. Calculated as `initCollateral / initMarginReq`. Reflects how much initial margin capacity remains before new positions are restricted. When this falls below `1`, the account cannot open new positions or borrow more.
